title: Export sanitized CSV/JSON public tables (deterministic build + schema v1)
author: Mei Lin
description: Context: Marketing/docs need a stable, reproducible “public subset” of benchmark results to power the report landing page and PDF charts. Today we only have the raw internal table export (includes internal-only fields, non-stable ordering, and run identifiers) which is not suitable for publication or repeatable builds. This PR adds a deterministic export pipeline that produces versioned CSV/JSON tables + a manifest, with explicit redaction and schema validation. What this adds: (1) `export_public_tables` module that reads the aggregated benchmark results artifact and writes `dist/public_tables/v1/` in both CSV and JSON formats; (2) schema v1 (`schema/public_table_schema_v1.json`) with required fields + units and display names; (3) deterministic build controls: stable sorting, fixed float formatting/rounding, UTC timestamps, explicit newline handling, and exclusion of non-deterministic metadata; (4) redaction rules to guarantee no internal identifiers leak (request IDs, run UUIDs, hostnames, GPU IDs, cluster names, per-customer tiers, internal pricing components); (5) a `MANIFEST.json` with checksums per output file, plus `BUILD_INFO.json` containing only safe metadata (git SHA, export version, input artifact hash). Public outputs: `public_table_chat_latency_per_dollar_v1.csv/json` and `public_table_embeddings_latency_per_dollar_v1.csv/json` (one row per {model, region, workload, context_length_bucket, output_length_bucket, concurrency_profile}). Each file includes p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens (or per 1M embedding tokens), and derived latency_per_dollar with units. Determinism notes: We sort rows by (workload, model_family, model, region, concurrency_profile, context_bucket, output_bucket). Floats are formatted with a fixed quantization (latency_ms: 1 decimal, throughput_tps: 2 decimals, cost_per_1m_tokens_usd: 4 decimals, latency_per_dollar_ms_per_usd: 2 decimals). JSON is emitted with sorted keys and stable indentation; CSV uses RFC4180 quoting and LF newlines. Build entrypoints: `make public-tables` and `python -m benchmark_lab.export_public_tables --input <results.json> --out dist/public_tables --schema schema/public_table_schema_v1.json --version v1`. CI: Adds a job that runs export on a pinned fixture input and asserts byte-for-byte equality against golden outputs (to catch accidental non-determinism). Checklist: [x] Output contains only approved public fields (no internal IDs) [x] Schema validation passes [x] Deterministic build test added [x] Docs snippet added for downstream consumers (Docs/Marketing) [x] Linked to ENG-2872. Follow-ups (not in this PR): wire this into the report build pipeline + landing page PR; add a small “public table diff” helper for reviewers when results refresh.
commits: export: add public table exporter with redaction + schema validation
schema: introduce public_table_schema_v1 with units and required fields
build: add make target + deterministic golden test fixture
docs: add downstream usage notes + example load script
checks: CI summary: ✅ unit-tests (py3.11) | ✅ lint (ruff) | ✅ typecheck (pyright) | ✅ public-table-determinism (golden) | ✅ schema-validate (v1) | ✅ package-build. Notable: first run of `public-table-determinism` failed due to locale-dependent float formatting; fixed by forcing `LC_ALL=C` in the workflow and using Decimal quantization in the exporter.
conversation: Claire Dubois (review): Can we guarantee the exporter never includes run-level identifiers? I see `run_id` in the internal table sometimes. Also please confirm we’re not leaking region-internal cluster naming. Mei Lin (author): Yep—exporter uses an explicit allowlist (`public_table_field_allowlist_v1.txt`). `run_id`, `cluster`, `host`, `gpu_type`, `instance_id`, `price_component_breakdown`, and `customer_tier` are dropped even if present in the input. Added a unit test that asserts none of these keys exist anywhere in the JSON output; and a regex guard for hostname-like values in CSV. Sana Farid (review): Rounding: for the report we need stable numbers, but we also need to avoid rounding errors changing rank order. Can we include both a display value and a raw value? Mei Lin (author): We discussed this with Perf/Evals—keeping a single value per metric in the public artifact is preferable to avoid confusion. Export uses fixed quantization but computed on full precision first. Added `notes_precision.md` section in README explaining rounding policy and that comparisons should use confidence/variance language per guidelines. Nadia Rahman (review): Cost metric naming: `cost_per_1m_tokens_usd` is fine for chat, but embeddings are often counted differently. Can we make sure units are explicit? Mei Lin (author): Added `cost_unit` field per workload (`usd_per_1m_input_tokens` for chat; `usd_per_1m_embedding_tokens` for embeddings) and clarified in schema + README. Tyler Benson (review): Marketing needs a single predictable path and versioning. Suggest `dist/public_tables/<version>/` with a manifest and a stable filename map. Mei Lin (author): Implemented `dist/public_tables/v1/` + `MANIFEST.json` + stable filenames. Also added `BUILD_INFO.json` and checksum verification script. Claire Dubois (final): Looks good. Please add a short section on how downstream can diff tables between refreshes (even if just using MANIFEST + checksums). Mei Lin (author): Added to README: compare MANIFEST checksums + file diff, and included `scripts/validate_public_tables.sh` for sanity checks. Approved. Merge: Squash merged into `main` after CI green.
release_notes: Internal-only: Adds deterministic generation of sanitized public benchmark tables (CSV/JSON) for Marketing/Docs consumption; no runtime behavior changes.
